Definition: from a compound of G3844 and G3551; to be opposed to law, i.e. to transgress:--contrary to law.
BiblicalUsage: Paranomeo means acting contrary to law. Paul uses it once, in Acts 23:3, when the high priest orders him struck: Paul says the man sits to judge him after the law, yet commands him to be smitten contrary to the law.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a judge who breaks the law he claims to uphold has already condemned himself.
